description: Nine-panel EBSD composite from a Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si low-density steel tensile-deformed at three temperatures; every map carries a 100 µm or 20 µm scale bar. (a-c) are inverse pole figure (IPF) maps, each with a colour triangle labelled 001, 101, 111 plus AD and RD arrows; only (a) (-196 °C) contains white arrows marking mechanical twins, while (b) (-77 °C) and (c) (RT) have none. (d-f) are grain-boundary (GB) maps with dashed frames labelled g, h and (in f) an unreadable letter; legends give LAGB (2-15°) and HAGB (>15°) fractions: 70.2%/29.8% in (d, -196 °C), 63.0%/37.0% in (e, -77 °C) and 56.0%/44.0% in (f, RT), so the low-angle boundary fraction rises sharply as deformation temperature falls. (g-i) are the framed regions of (d-f) shown as kernel-average-misorientation (captioned as GND distribution) maps superposed on GB maps, with a colour bar reading "Kernel Aver. Misorient. [°]" from 0 to 3. Together the panels show that lowering the tensile temperature raises the LAGB fraction and local misorientation accumulation, with mechanical twinning appearing only at -196 °C.

observations.observation: Panel (a) IPF map (-196 °C) contains white arrows marking mechanical twins; (b) (-77 °C) and (c) (RT) carry no such arrows.
The GB map (d) legend states LAGB 2-15° = 70.2% and HAGB >15° = 29.8% for the -196 °C sample.
The GB map (e) legend states LAGB 2-15° = 63.0% and HAGB >15° = 37.0% for the -77 °C sample.
The GB map (f) legend states LAGB 2-15° = 56.0% and HAGB >15° = 44.0% for the RT sample.

The printed LAGB fractions 70.2% (-196 °C) > 63.0% (-77 °C) > 56.0% (RT) show the low-angle boundary fraction increasing as deformation temperature decreases, with HAGB fraction following the opposite order (29.8%, 37.0%, 44.0%).
Panels (g-i) each carry a colour bar labelled 'Kernel Aver. Misorient.' with ticks 0, 1, 2, 3 in degrees, and a 20 µm scale bar (versus 100 µm in a-f).
The dashed square frames in (d), (e) and (f) are labelled g, h and an unreadable letter respectively, linking each to the corresponding magnified map (g), (h) and (i).

The caption states the panels are EBSD analyses of the experimental steel deformed at (a,d,g) -196 °C, (b,e,h) -77 °C and (c,f,i) RT, with (a-c) IPF maps, (d-f) GB maps and (g-i) GND distribution maps superposed with GB maps for the framed regions of (d-f).
The caption states that in the IPF maps the colours indicate crystal directions parallel to the tensile direction, and that mechanical twins are marked with arrows.
The caption states that in the grain boundary maps the fractions of LAGBs and HAGBs are marked in red and black colours; the visible legends in (d-f) use red for 2-15° and blue for >15°.
The citing text states that the crystal orientation of the deformed austenite grains concentrates in {111} and {001} as a result of coordinated plastic deformation.
The citing text states that the fraction of LAGBs dramatically increases with decreasing temperature, and that LAGBs mainly concentrate at austenite grains with finer grain size.
The citing text states that GNDs accumulate at LAGBs, indicating more severe local deformation of these regions, and that no mechanical twins but microbands occur at -77 °C.

subfigures.description: IPF map of the -196 °C tensile-deformed sample, 100 µm scale bar; inset colour triangle labelled 001/101/111 with AD and RD arrows. Three-four white arrows mark elongated features identified as mechanical twins.
IPF map of the -77 °C sample, 100 µm scale bar; same 001/101/111 triangle orientation key implied. No arrow-marked twins.
IPF map of the RT sample, 100 µm scale bar; coloured grains with no arrow annotations.
GB map of the -196 °C sample, 100 µm scale bar; legend red line = 2-15° (70.2%), blue line = >15° (29.8%); dashed rectangular frame labelled g in the lower-centre region.
GB map of the -77 °C sample, 100 µm scale bar; legend 2-15° = 63.0%, >15° = 37.0%; dashed frame labelled h right of centre.
GB map of the RT sample, 100 µm scale bar; legend 2-15° = 56.0%, >15° = 44.0%; dashed frame at the upper-left, its letter label not reliably legible.

Kernel average misorientation (captioned GND) map superposed with GB map for the framed region of (d), 20 µm scale bar; colour bar 0-3° 'Kernel Aver. Misorient.'; high-misorientation red/orange concentrated along intra-granular bands.
Same map type for the framed region of (e), 20 µm scale bar; 0-3° colour bar; red/orange high-misorientation regions decorating boundaries and slip/microband traces.
Same map type for the framed region of (f), 20 µm scale bar; 0-3° colour bar; denser network of black high-angle boundaries with finer red misorientation decoration.

IPF colour triangles are drawn only in panel (a); orientation key for (b) and (c) is assumed identical but not printed in those panels
